title: Merged findings
description: The single file the main session reads each round. It groups what the two legs reported, records where they agree and where they contradict each other, and carries forward what the ledger already decided.

stale.description: True when a reviewer's start and end digests disagree, so the tree moved while it was reading. Stale findings still get reported; the round does not count as clean.

id.description: Run-stable identifier, F-001 onward. Assigned once and reused in every later round so the ledger can track a decision across rounds.

state.description: regression means a finding recorded as fixed came back. reraised_after_rejection means a reviewer refiled something rejected with evidence, so read prior.evidence before spending time on it.

severity.description: The highest severity any source assigned. Each source keeps its own value in sources[].

agreement.description: both when the two legs independently found this, otherwise the name of the only leg that did. An unconfirmed finding is not a wrong one, but it deserves more scrutiny before you change code.

blocking.description: Computed, not judged: severity is not minor, and either confidence is at least 0.6 or agreement is both. Convergence is measured on these.

contradiction.description: Id of an item whose premise this one denies. One of the two is wrong, which makes the pair the cheapest thing to resolve first.

prior.description: The ledger decision this item repeats, copied in so the main session can re-read its own reasoning without opening state.json.

dropped.description: Exact duplicates only. Judging a finding false is the main session's call, so nothing else may be removed here.

raw.description: Findings read from the reviewer reports. It must equal items plus dropped, which is how a silently lost finding is caught.

degraded.description: Legs that did not return a usable report. A non-empty list forbids a clean verdict, however few findings the other leg returned.
